thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: multi-node swarm-sync failure detected — 4 nodes reporting GPU communicator errors, alarm threshold crossed (5xx spike). Please ack and join #incidents.
oncall-aya: acked. jumping on. can someone paste the errors?
runtime-eli: seeing repeated: \"NCCL_COMM_FATAL_ERROR\" and quick CUDA Xid messages on nodes gpu-az3-07,gpu-az3-08,gpu-az2-11,gpu-az2-12. container exits with status 137 then restarts.
eng-nat: logs attached — brief snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T02:15:03Z] NCCL WARN Transport : nvlink error on rank 2
[2026-03-17T02:15:03Z] NCCL ERROR NCCL_COMM_FATAL_ERROR: aborted by system
[2026-03-17T02:15:03Z] cuda: Fatal Xid 79 on GPU 0
```
sre-omar: looks like driver crash (Xid 79) followed by container OOM killer on some pods. are these ephemeral nodes or reserved?
ops-lee: these are ephemeral burst nodes in the inference-swarm pool (auto-scale). recent kernel update applied last night on az3 hosts — rolling window shows 3 hosts with updated nvidia driver 525.x.
ml-zoe: customer impact: we have 2 customers on dedicated routes that saw 502s and an internal SLA alert. estimate ~4% of traffic fell back to single-GPU-serving causing increased latency for those requests.
pm-jordan: P0? do we need to page customers? status page already showing degraded for inference.redwood.ai
oncall-aya: triaging: runtime-eli, can you try isolating one host and run a controlled repro on a staging task? i'd prefer we cordon unaffected nodes first.
runtime-eli: starting checklist from runbook /runbooks/multi-gpu-sync.md: cordon affected nodes -> drain pods -> collect /var/log/nvidia* + dmesg -> attempt graceful container restart -> if persists, force-driver-reload.
eng-nat: i'm seeing repeated OOMs inside the torch worker before the driver crash on az2-11. memory footprint spiking when sequence lengths > 2048. could be KV cache thrash + pinned memory leak.
sre-omar: action: cordon gpu-az3-07 and gpu-az2-11 now, draining traffic.
ops-lee: cordoned and drained. pods evicted; auto-scaler started to bring up replacements in dedicated-east-1.
ml-zoe: routing change: switching heavy pipeline-parallel jobs to fallback model variant 'rpl-light-1g' for 10m to avoid large KV caches. notify API gateway.
oncall-aya: doing live debug on gpu-az3-08. attaching to container shows this in stderr:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): nccl_comm failure: unhandled error
Aborted (core dumped)
```
runtime-eli: core dumps collected to /tmp/incident-5581209876/cores. grabbing driver logs and container env.
eng-nat: quick mitigation: enforce token-level batching limit to reduce max sequence on the fly and push a configuration to the router: max_seq=1024 for swarm pool.
pm-jordan: customer comms: drafting status update — \"Degraded inference in US-west. We are routing traffic to alternate capacity and applying mitigations. No data loss.\" anyone see request-level errors that contain PII in logs? we must avoid exposing.
sre-omar: logs scrubbed. no PII surfaced. good.
ops-lee: kernel & driver correlation looks suspicious — az3 hosts have 525.116, az2 still on 525.102. 3 of 4 failures on 525.116. rolling nodes back not possible quickly; prefer to fallback traffic.
ml-zoe: started canary traffic on dedicated-east-1, success so far: 200/200 for 1k requests. latency within SLO.
oncall-aya: summary so far: cause suspected interplay between driver version + large KV cache usage causing cuda driver resets -> nccl communicator aborts -> container restarts. impact: ~4-6% of inference traffic in US-west degraded, 2 customers reporting timeouts. mitigation: cordon drained effected hosts, rerouted burst traffic to dedicated cluster, enforced seq cap and model fallback.
eng-nat: next steps: collect kernel traces, submit driver bug to vendor with core dump and repro. create a postmortem ticket and link runbook gaps (auto-detect driver-version skew earlier).
pm-jordan: i'm going to publish a short status page update in 10m. timeline for recovery estimate?
runtime-eli: immediate: traffic rerouted + seq cap in place -> should be low risk in 5-10m. full remediation depends on vendor patch / driver rollback coordination, ETA 6-12h.
ml-zoe: can we add a temporary heuristic to avoid multi-gpu placement for jobs that hit seq > 1024 until this is solved?
ops-lee: yes, adding placement rule now: prefer single-gpu for sequences > 1024 on swarm pool. pushing policy.
oncall-aya: thanks. handing off to night oncall at 23:30UTC — keep monitoring, preserve artifacts, create post-incident timeline. assign follow-ups: @runtime-eli collect repro and file ticket, @eng-nat draft root-cause, @ops-lee coordinate rollback plan with infra.
incident-bot: incident updated: status=mitigated, mitigation=traffic_reroute+seq_cap, owners=[runtime-eli,eng-nat,ops-lee], severity=high
pm-jordan: noted. i'll include customer notes and link to the follow-up spreadsheet.
eng-nat: one reminder — add a small test to CI that exposes driver skew (bootstrap on both driver minor versions). i'll open a PR.
oncall-aya: final: leaving the channel for now. thx everyone for the rapid response. :heart:
